papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) extensive genomic heterogeneity and immunosuppressive tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) are major factors contributing to treatment resistance. This study aims to elucidate the molecular mechanisms by which Robustic Acid 4-O-amino substituted synthetic derivatives (MF1), a novel robustic acid derivative, derived from structural modifications of natural products from Dalbergia benthamii Prain, targets carcinogenic signaling and synergistically regulates the crosstalk between autophagy and ferroptosis to induce programmed cell death in HCC. In vitro functional assays confirmed that MF1 exhibits significant antitumor activity. Mechanistically, MF1 significantly upregulates cellular oxidative stress levels, inducing characteristic changes in mitochondrial ultrastructure and apoptosis; simultaneously, by promoting intracellular Fe²⁺ accumulation and downregulating the expression of key ferroptosis regulators GPX4 and SLC7A11, it potently activates the ferroptosis process. Concurrently, MF1 continuously activates the cytotoxic autophagy pathway by regulating the LC3 I/II conversion ratio and upregulating the expression of core autophagy proteins ATG5 and Beclin-1. Network pharmacology identified 7 core targets of MF1 that are common to both ferroptosis and autophagy regulation. qPCR validation showed that MF1 significantly downregulated the mRNA expression of these 7 core oncogenes in HepG2 cells. Molecular docking confirmed strong binding affinities between MF1 and five core targets, 100 ns all-atom molecular dynamics simulations further validated the conformational stability of all five top-ranked MF1-protein complexes, with the higher binding stability for AKT1, SRC and MTOR. In summary, this study clarifies MF1 induces apoptosis and ferroptosis in HepG2 cells, suggesting its potential as a new therapeutic option for HCC.

papers.abstract: Anti-CD19 CAR T-cell therapy is the standard second-line treatment for patients with relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma. However, there is no evidence from randomised controlled trials in patients ineligible for transplantation. To address this gap, we compared zamtocabtagene autoleucel (zamto-cel), a CAR T-cell therapy directed at CD20 and CD19, with rituximab-gemcitabine-oxaliplatin (R-GemOx) chemoimmunotherapy in patients ineligible for transplantation with relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma. DALY 2-EU is an open-label, multicentre, randomised, phase 2 trial conducted at 45 centres across 12 countries in Europe. Eligible patients were adults (aged ≥18 years) with second-line relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma confirmed histologically who were ineligible for transplantation and had received first-line chemoimmunotherapy containing a combination of an anthracycline-based regimen and an anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody, with Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status score of 2 or less. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to zamto-cel (single intravenous infusion of 2·5 × 106 fresh (ie, non-cryopreserved) CAR T-cells per kg, capped at 100 kg, produced in a closed automated system) or R-GemOx (rituximab [375 mg/m2 intravenously on day 1], gemcitabine [1000 mg/m2 intravenously on day 1 or 2], and oxaliplatin [100 mg/m2 intravenously on day 1 or 2] administered for up to eight 14-day cycles). Randomisation was done with an interactive web response system and stratified by age, gender, lactate dehydrogenase, International Prognostic Index, histology, time to relapse after the start of first-line therapy, and country. The primary endpoint was event-free survival assessed by a masked independent review committee and compared all patients randomly assigned to the zamto-cel and R-GemOx groups using a one-sided log-rank test. Safety was assessed in all patients who received study treatment. This ongoing trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04844866). Between Oct 14, 2021, and Jul 16, 2024, 219 patients were screened and 160 were randomly assigned to zamto-cel (n=82) and R-GemOx (n=78). The median age was 74·0 years (IQR 70·5-77·0). Patients were predominantly male (100 [63%] of 160 were men and 60 [38%] women) and White (91 [57%]), with race not reported for 64 (40%). Median vein-to-vein time for zamto-cel was 15 days (IQR 15-16). With a median follow-up of 17·0 months (IQR 9·0-22·8), event-free survival was longer in the zamto-cel group than in the R-GemOx group (6·21 months [95% CI 3·84-13·77] vs 2·53 months [1·97-3·35]; HR 0·39 [95% CI 0·27-0·58]; p<0·0001). Grade 3 or higher treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 63 (83%) of 76 with zamto-cel and in 65 (86%) of 76 with R-GemOx. The most common grade 3-4 adverse events were neutropenia (28 [37%] with zamto-cel and 17 [22%] with R-GemOx), anaemia (11 [14%] and 12 [16%]), and decreased neutrophil count (20 [26%] and seven [9%]). Serious adverse events occurred in 31 (41%) patients with zamto-cel and 50 (66%) with R-GemOx, most commonly malignant neoplasm progression (11 [14%] and 38 [50%]), cytokine release syndrome (CRS; six [8%] and none), and immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (four [5%] and none). Treatment-related deaths occurred in two (3%) of 82 patients with zamto-cel (due to CRS and haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis) and in one (1%) of 78 with R-GemOx (malignant lymphoma progression). The risk-benefit ratio observed in the DALY 2-EU study supports consideration of zamto-cel as a second-line standard treatment option for patients with relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma who are ineligible for transplantation. papers.abstract: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) drives intestinal barrier dysfunction, endotoxemia, and liver injury, yet the epithelial mechanisms remain undefined. Autophagy and lysosomes maintain intestinal epithelial homoeostasis and barrier integrity, but their response to chronic alcohol exposure is unclear. Human intestinal tissues from individuals with and without AUD were analysed alongside human intestinal organoids. Wild-type, CAG-RFP-EGFP-LC3, GFP-LC3B, and Atg16l1 hypomorphic mice underwent chronic-binge ethanol feeding. Organoids and Caco-2 cells were exposed to ethanol (50 mM) with or without bafilomycin A1 or Torin-2. Autophagy-lysosome pathways were assessed using transcriptomics, immunofluorescence, biochemical fractionation, and flux reporters. Alcohol induced heterogeneous autophagy-lysosome responses characterised by lysosomal stress/adaptive remodelling. These changes occurred with limited autophagosome formation and maturation, resulting in impaired autophagic throughput. These responses differed along the crypt-villus axis and between intestinal regions. Disrupted autophagy was associated with altered trafficking and accumulation of claudin-2. Atg16l1 hypomorphic mice exhibited increased baseline intestinal permeability vs wild-type controls (p = 0.03). Following ethanol exposure, Atg16l1 hypomorphic mice showed greater intestinal permeability (p = 0.003), circulating and hepatic endotoxin (p = 0.002), hepatic triglycerides (p = 0.01), and serum ALT (p = 0.02) vs ethanol-fed wild-type mice. Alcohol disrupts intestinal autophagy-lysosome homoeostasis in a spatially heterogeneous manner, accompanied by defective epithelial proteostasis and tight junction dysregulation. Impaired autophagosome formation exacerbates gut permeability and liver injury, supporting intestinal autophagy as a potential therapeutic target in alcohol-associated disease. Broader applicability of the human findings requires validation in larger cohorts. This study was supported by grants from the National Institutes of Health.

papers.abstract: Human brain cellular xenograft (HBCX) models are emerging as a platform to study human brain physiology and pathology in vivo. HBCXs involve transplanting human pluripotent stem cell-derived neurons, glia, or organoids into immunodeficient mice to model human disease. These models have revealed human-specific cellular and molecular phenotypes, developmental trajectories, and disease mechanisms that would otherwise be inaccessible in traditional in vitro systems and animal models. They also provide a scalable, genetically editable framework for functional genomics studies, drug testing, and biomarker discovery. Given the pronounced species differences in microglia and other tissue-resident brain macrophages and their central involvement in neurodegenerative disease, these models also provide an in vivo platform to interrogate human neuroimmunology. In selected settings, they may help guide future cell-based therapeutic strategies. This review provides an overview of the current applications, discusses the challenges and limitations, and highlights future avenues of HBCXs in neuroimmunology and translational research.

papers.abstract: This phase 2 trial included 211 Chinese participants with type 2 diabetes mellitus (mean age 48.4 years; 131 participants were male). Participants received once-weekly subcutaneous UBT251 (2 mg, 4 mg [initial dose 0.5 mg], 4 mg [initial dose 1 mg], or 6 mg), 1 mg semaglutide, or placebo for 24 weeks. At week 24, UBT251 achieved least-squares mean changes in glycated hemoglobin of -2.16% (95% CI, -2.39 to -1.92) to -1.98% (95% CI, -2.31 to -1.64), versus -1.77% (95% CI, -1.99 to -1.54) for semaglutide and -0.66% (95% CI, -0.90 to -0.41) for placebo (placebo-adjusted differences: -1.50% to -1.32%; all p < 0.001). UBT251 significantly reduced fasting blood glucose, 2-h postprandial glucose, and waist circumference versus placebo (all p < 0.001). Weight reduction with UBT251 was significantly greater than both placebo and semaglutide (all p < 0.05). Gastrointestinal events were the most common treatment-emergent adverse events. These findings support further phase 3 evaluation of UBT251. Registration: CTR20250029; NCT07163624.

papers.abstract: Whether intestinal fungal dysbiosis contributes to hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) progression and resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) remains unclear. We investigated how gut Candida albicans influences HCC progression, immune remodeling, and response to ICI therapy. Fecal and tumor samples from patients with HCC, liver cirrhosis, and healthy controls were analyzed using ITS2 sequencing, immune profiling, and correlation analyses. Mechanistic studies focused on four complementary autochthonous murine HCC models and cell-based assays, integrating single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing, genetic and pharmacologic perturbations, Kaede photoconversion, fungal antigen recall assays, antifungal treatment, and anti-PD-1 therapy. Fecal C. albicans abundance was higher in HCC patients and was associated with advanced disease, shorter overall survival, and reduced durable clinical benefit. Across HCC models, C. albicans gavage increased tumor burden and induced a Th17/IL-17A-skewed microenvironment characterized by Trem2+ macrophage accumulation and impaired CD8+ T cell infiltration and function. Antifungal treatment attenuated tumor progression, whereas IL-17A blockade or deficiency largely abrogated C. albicans-associated tumor promotion. Mechanistically, IL-17A induced tumor-derived MCP-1 through ACT1-TRAF6-TAK1 signaling to recruit macrophages and upregulated PAI-1, which activated TGF-β/Smad3 signaling to promote an immunosuppressive Trem2+ macrophage state. These macrophages limited CD8+ T cell recruitment and effector function through coordinated CXCL10 repression and GAL-1 induction, while potentially reinforcing Th17 responses through IL-1β and IL-6. Kaede photoconversion demonstrated enhanced mesenteric lymph node-to-liver Th17 trafficking, while fungal antigen recall assays revealed preferential Th17 responsiveness to C. albicans. C. albicans also impaired anti-PD-1 efficacy in vivo, whereas antifungal treatment partially restored therapeutic responsiveness. Intestinal C. albicans promotes HCC progression and anti-PD-1 resistance through an IL-17A-Trem2+ macrophage circuit, supporting its potential as a biomarker and therapeutic target. Intestinal fungal dysbiosis is increasingly recognized as a component of the gut-liver axis, but its functional contribution to HCC has remained poorly defined. Our study identifies intestinal Candida albicans as a promoter of HCC progression in experimental models and delineates an IL-17A-MCP-1/PAI-1-Trem2+ macrophage circuit that links fungal exposure to impaired CD8+ T-cell immunity and reduced response to PD-1 blockade. These findings are relevant to researchers and clinicians seeking microbiome-associated determinants of HCC progression and immunotherapy resistance. Fecal C. albicans abundance and components of this immune circuit may warrant evaluation as biomarkers for patient stratification and as potential targets for combination therapy. However, the clinical associations reported here are based on modest observational cohorts, and antifungal treatment was tested as a proof-of-concept intervention in mice. Larger prospective studies and more selective therapeutic approaches will therefore be required before these findings can inform clinical management.

papers.abstract: Mucin-16 (MUC16) is overexpressed in >60% of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) cases and correlates with poor outcomes, yet its role in regulating tumor-immune interactions remains incompletely defined. Using KPC and KPC-MUC16 knockout (KPC-MUC16KO) genetically engineered and orthotopic mouse models, we show that loss of MUC16 markedly reduces tumor burden and reprograms the tumor microenvironment (TME) toward a less immunosuppressive state. MUC16 deficiency significantly decreased CD206+ and Ym1/2+ M2-like macrophages, increased the M1/M2 ratio, and improved survival. Cytokine profiling identified CCL2 and Serpin-E1 as MUC16- dependent secreted factors that promote macrophage recruitment and polarization; neutralization of these cytokines reduced macrophage migration in vitro. Bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDM) exposed to MUC16-expressing tumor cells or conditioned media adopted a CD206+Arg1+ M2-like phenotype, whereas MUC16KO tumor signals favored inflammatory CD86+iNOS+ M1-like polarization. Macrophage depletion using clodronate liposomes significantly impaired tumor growth in MUC16-competent tumors but had minimal effect in KPC-MUC16KO tumors, indicating dependence on macrophage-mediated immunosuppression in the former group. Spatial transcriptomics revealed a globally distinct TME in MUC16KO tumors, including enhanced antigen-presentation programs, increased complement activation, and fibroblast states skewed toward pro-inflammatory signaling. These findings establish MUC16 as a key orchestrator of macrophage-driven immunosuppression in PDAC and support therapeutic strategies combining MUC16-targeted interventions with TME-reprogramming approaches.

papers.abstract: The role of neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) in patients with upper tract urothelial carcinoma (UTUC) remains controversial, mainly because of the lack of high-level evidence. We aim to update the evidence on NAC regarding pathological and oncological outcomes in patients with nonmetastatic UTUC. Moreover, we also aimed to give an overview of neoadjuvant immunotherapy (NAI) in the current clinical scenario. A systematic review of 41 studies on NAC and NAI (eight prospective studies [PS] or randomized clinical trials [RCTs] and 33 retrospective studies [RS]) was conducted according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. Outcomes of interest included pathological complete response (pCR), pathological partial response (pPR), pathological downstaging, overall survival (OS), cancer-specific survival (CSS), and disease-free survival (DFS). Pooled analyses were performed using effect sizes for pathological outcomes and hazard ratios (HRs) for survival outcomes. Finally, 5-yr proportions were summarized when a 5-yr time threshold was available. Of the 41 articles, 30 (five PS or RCTs and 25 RS) were eligible for meta-analysis (n = 2384 patients). The pooled pCR, pPR, and pathological downstaging rates were, respectively, 11% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 10-12), 44% (95% CI: 38-50), and 20% (95% CI: 10-37). Compared with radical nephroureterectomy (RNU), NAC was associated with pooled HRs of 0.56 (95% CI: 0.39-0.80) for OS, 0.47 (95% CI: 0.26-0.85) for CSS, and 0.55 (95% CI: 0.24-1.26) for DFS. Evidence on NAI remains limited in terms of sample size and is primarily derived from early-phase studies. NAC was associated with favorable oncological outcomes compared with RNU alone. Nevertheless, the absence of prospective randomized studies limits the strength of the evidence, and further high-quality trials are warranted to confirm these findings.

papers.abstract: Subsets of intestinal CD4+ T cells directly recognize commensal bacteria and coordinate tolerance versus protective immunity. Our limited understanding of CD4+ T cell specificities and corresponding functional phenotypes has created a barrier to deciphering the mechanisms of mucosal homeostasis and inflammation mediated by the adaptive immune system. To address this, we leveraged an immunodominant Bacteroidetes epitope in SusC to perform single-cell profiling of the SusC-specific and total CD4+ T cell landscapes in intestinal tissues of patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). By analyzing phenotypes and T cell receptor specificities in parallel, we uncovered phenotypic diversification of T helper 17 (Th17) cells in IBD and identified an epithelial-localized, SusC-reactive Th17 subset that is BACH2lo, GZMAhi, and expresses the costimulatory receptor TMIGD2. Together, our results highlight the utility of tracking commensal-specific T cell responses to define specialized subsets of Th17 cells associated with loss of tolerance to the microbiome.

papers.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) remains one of the most common serious complications after noncardiac surgery, and intraoperative hypotension (IOH) is consistently identified as a modifiable risk factor. Observational studies show a consistent, roughly dose-response association between IOH, particularly at mean arterial pressures below 60-65 mmHg, and postoperative AKI, with stronger associations in patients with limited renal reserve. Definitions of IOH vary widely, which complicates the comparison of studies and the translation of thresholds into clinical targets. Randomized trials of individualized or higher blood pressure targets have generally not confirmed a kidney-protective benefit, and pooled analyses with trial sequential analysis have not demonstrated that higher targets reduce AKI. This narrative review examines how IOH definitions evolved, summarizes the conflicting intervention evidence, and assesses the controversies that shape current practice. The review concludes that avoiding severe and sustained hypotension remains reasonable, whereas current randomized trial evidence does not support a general kidney-protective benefit of higher or individualized blood pressure targets. This conclusion is provisional and is tempered by the methodologic and causal uncertainties.

papers.abstract: We report the preclinical and early clinical evaluation of in vivo genome editing for Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD), delivered via a single AAV9 vector. In humanized DMD mice, systemic administration achieved targeted genome editing, partial dystrophin restoration, and improved muscle function. In non-human primates, efficient on-target editing was achieved with no dose-limiting toxicity identified under the conditions tested. In an open-label, dose-escalation, first-in-human clinical trial (NCT06594094), post-treatment muscle biopsies provided early molecular evidence of hfCas12Max-mediated genome editing and detectable dystrophin expression in participants with DMD. However, at the higher dose level (1.0 × 1014 vg/kg), one participant experienced a treatment-related fatal serious adverse event, characterized by marked complement activation and systemic cytokine response shortly after dosing. This work provides initial human proof-of-concept for muscle genome editing while crucially highlighting the critical role of immunologic risks and the narrow therapeutic window of systemic adeno-associated virus (AAV)-CRISPR therapies, underscoring the need to develop safer dosing and immunomodulation strategies.

papers.abstract: To prospectively explore efficacy and safety of radiotherapy combined with albumin-bound paclitaxel and platinum-based chemotherapy for locoregional recurrent cervical cancer (CC). Patients with locoregional recurrent CC were enrolled in the analysis. The enrolled patients received radiotherapy and albumin-bound paclitaxel and platinum-based chemotherapy. The primary endpoint was overall survival (OS). Secondary endpoints were progression-free survival (PFS), objective response rate (ORR), and safety. 99 patients were enrolled. For all patients, the 3-year PFS and 3-year OS were 48.5% and 58.6%. 17.2% of patients achieved CR and 67.7% of patients achieved PR. The ORR was 84.8%. Moreover, 10.1% of patients were confirmed SD. The DCR was 94.9%. Locoregional recurrent CC could benefit from radiotherapy combined with albumin-bound paclitaxel and platinum-based chemotherapy.

papers.abstract: Chemotherapy and pembrolizumab treatment can improve survival in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), but data are limited in older adults. We examined treatment patterns, efficacy, and safety for older patients on pembrolizumab for early-stage (eTNBC) and metastatic TNBC (mTNBC). Through medical record review, we collected tumor, treatment, and outcome data for patients ≥ 65 years receiving pembrolizumab-containing therapy for TNBC between 2021 and 2024. For all, we examined immune related adverse events (irAEs) and hospitalizations. For eTNBC, we examined percent ideal dose, treatment discontinuation, and factors associated with pathologic complete response (pCR). Among patients with mTNBC, progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were analyzed using Kaplan-Meier methods. Among 136 included patients, median age was 71 (range 63-91); 85 had eTNBC, of whom 42% received the neoadjuvant KEYNOTE-522 regimen. There were 51 with mTNBC who received a variety of regimens. In eTNBC, mean ideal dose was 82%, 43% had a pCR, 41% were hospitalized, 39% experienced irAEs, and 4% had treatment-related deaths. Patients aged > 70 had more irAEs, and lower % ideal dose. No clinical or treatment variables were associated with pCR. In mTNBC, 43% were hospitalized, 18% were admitted to the ICU, and 41% experienced irAEs. With a median follow-up of 29 months, median PFS was 5.45 months (95% CI, 3.8-7.8), and median OS was 23.1 months (95% CI, 18.6-35.4). In this cohort of older adults with TNBC receiving pembrolizumab-containing treatment, we observed high rates of serious toxicity, with lower-than-expected pCR rates in eTNBC, and short OS in mTNBC. Not applicable.

papers.abstract: Infiltrating lobular carcinoma (ILC) accounts for ~ 10% of all invasive breast cancer histologies. ILC is associated with worse prognosis than infiltrating ductal cancer. Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) are commonly elevated in metastatic breast cancer (mBC) and elevated levels of CTCs are associated with worse prognosis in breast cancers. We investigated CTC incidence in ILC in two patient cohorts. Data from electronic medical records at the University of Michigan were identified using the EMERSE search engine to assess CTC levels in patients with mBC, using CellSearch®. Findings were validated in a separate cohort of mBC patients who participated in a research protocol where CTC were analyzed. Within the EMERSE cohort of 218, 38 (17%), 29 (13%) and 151 (69%) patients, had lobular, mixed, and ductal mBC subtype, respectively. Overall, 101/218 (46%) patients had elevated CTC (≥ 5/7.5 ml whole blood). In this cohort, patients with ILC were more likely to have elevated CTCs (28/38; 74%) compared to those with mixed (14/29; 48%) or ductal (59/151; 39%) mBC (p = 0.001). In multivariate regression, patients with ILC were seven times more likely than ductal mBC to have elevated CTCs. These data were validated in 146 separate mBC patients in the research cohort. Elevated CTCs were detected in 79%, 31%, and 36% of patients with lobular, mixed and ductal mBC, respectively. CTC are more commonly elevated and tend to be higher in magnitude in patients with lobular compared to ductal mBC. CTC levels in mixed ductal-lobular morphology numerically more resemble ductal mBC.

papers.abstract: Sentinel lymph node biopsies (SLNBs) carry risk. Therefore, refinement of sentinel lymph node (SLN) identification protocols may improve patient safety. Currently, the 10 % Geiger count threshold is standard for SLN identification, yet the utility of more restrictive thresholds remains unexplored. This study explored whether a 30 % threshold could maintain diagnostic reliability while reducing the number of nodes removed. A single-institution, retrospective review of all malignant melanoma patients who underwent SLNB with technetium-99m sulfur colloid (99mTc) lymphatic mapping with or without methylene blue dye was performed. Only patients with at least two SLNs, preoperative clinical staging, and reported final pathology were considered for analysis. Individual SLN Geiger counts were calculated as fractions of the highest count value (percent hottest node [PHN]) found in the associated LN basin. Positive and negative predictive values were calculated and compared for the cohort using the gold standard 10 % and experimental 30 % Geiger count thresholds. Pathologic stage was determined for patients who had pathologically positive SLNs that remained unidentified by the 30 % count threshold. The study included 1,001 patients with 1,098 involved LN basins. Compared with the traditional 10 % threshold, the 30% threshold was associated with a higher positive predictive value and a comparable negative predictive value across all LN basins sampled and upon stratification by tumor preoperative T stage. The optimal Geiger count threshold was calculated to be 52.3 % for this cohort. In this exploratory retrospective review, a 30 % Geiger count threshold appeared to identify SLNs without compromising disease detection. These results suggest that higher thresholds may suffice for accurate staging and merit prospective evaluation.

papers.abstract: Our objective was to investigate whether cryptorchidism independently influenced cancer-specific survival (CSS) and overall survival in patients with testicular germ cell tumors (TGCTs). We conducted a cohort study using the Surveillance Epidemiology and End Results (SEER) database (2000-2022; 21 registries). Patients with TGCTs who underwent orchiectomy were identified and classified by primary site code as having descended (C62.1) or undescended (C62.0) testis. The final analytical cohort comprised 10,353 patients (10,103 descended, 250 undescended). Survival outcomes were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression adjusting for age, histology, stage, tumor size, race/ethnicity, and chemotherapy receipt. PSM (1:4 nearest neighbor) was performed as a sensitivity analysis to account for baseline differences between groups. Seminoma was significantly more prevalent in the undescended group (65.2% vs 51.4%; p < 0.001). Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated no significant difference in CSS between descended and undescended groups (log-rank p = 0.876). On multivariable Cox regression, cryptorchidism was not an independent predictor of CSS (hazard ratio [HR] 1.14; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.50-2.57; p = 0.762). Independent predictors of worse CSS included distant stage (HR 21.89; p < 0.001), nonseminoma histology (HR 3.11; p < 0.001), regional stage (HR 3.27; p < 0.001), older age (HR 1.04; p < 0.001), and Hispanic (HR 1.96; p < 0.001) and non-Hispanic Black race/ethnicity (HR 2.91; p < 0.001). Subgroup analyses by histology and stage consistently showed no survival difference. In the PSM cohort (249 vs 988), cryptorchidism remained non-significant (HR 1.55, 95% CI 0.60-3.95; p = 0.365; log-rank p = 0.62). Cryptorchidism was not independently associated with CSS or overall survival in patients with TGCTs. Prognosis and management should remain guided by established tumor-related prognostic and risk-stratification factors.

papers.abstract: Responses to chemotherapeutic agents vary substantially among patients with bladder cancer. The lack of preclinical models that accurately predict the clinical efficacy of intravesical chemotherapy remains a major barrier to precision oncology. In this prospective multicenter study (NCT06662071), 63 patients with bladder cancer were enrolled at four medical centers. Patient-derived organoids (PDOs) were established using specimens obtained by transurethral resection of bladder tumor. A total of 35 PDOs underwent high-throughput screening with a panel of eight clinically relevant chemotherapeutic agents. To identify the optimal classification strategy, we evaluated six distinct approaches by combining two statistical methods (the Jenks natural breaks method and the tertile method) with three sensitivity indicators (viability, nAUC, and IC50) and assessed the concordance between drug sensitivity profiles and real-world clinical follow-up data. We successfully established 41 PDOs. Comparative analysis indicated that post-digestion cell viability and total cell count may influence the success of PDO establishment. The PDOs showed high morphological and molecular concordance with the primary tumors. Among the six candidate strategies, IC50-Jenks showed the highest numerical concordance with clinical outcomes, with accuracy of 88.2% (95% CI, 63.6-98.5%) and specificity of 93.3% (95% CI, 68.1-99.8%). Representative case studies confirmed the utility of PDOs in identifying therapeutic futility and supporting the feasibility of bladder-sparing strategies. This multicenter feasibility study suggests that bladder cancer PDOs may support exploratory assessment of chemotherapy sensitivity. The proposed classification approach requires validation in larger, prospectively designed, clinically homogeneous cohorts before it can inform routine treatment decisions.

papers.abstract: Breast surgery and reconstruction rates in the USA continue to rise, with over 90% of new breast cancer diagnoses occurring in peri- or postmenopausal women. Despite the relevance of menopause to wound healing, postoperative outcomes in this population remain understudied. Estrogen hormone replacement therapy (HRT) may aid wound healing and menopausal symptoms, but carries prothrombotic risk. We investigate postsurgical outcomes after breast surgery and reconstruction among postmenopausal patients on HRTs compared to those without HRT use. Using the TriNetX database, we compared patients with and without HRT use within 1 year preceding breast reconstruction. Mastectomy and reconstruction procedures were identified using CPT codes. HRT use was identified using ICD-10 and RxNorm codes. Cohorts were propensity-matched for demographics and comorbidities. Risk differences with 95% confidence intervals were calculated for outcomes within 90 days postoperatively. Analyses were performed within TriNetX, with significance set at P < 0.05. Two cohorts were generated, with 3750 HRT+ and 75503 HRT- patients. After propensity matching, two cohorts of 3750 patients each were created. After propensity adjustment, there was no significant association between HRT use and postoperative mortality, VTE, or wound healing complications, which were comparably low across all surgery types. Among patients undergoing autologous reconstruction, 1-year revision rates were higher in the HRT+ cohort. Systemic hormone replacement therapy was not associated with an increased complications after breast reconstruction, including mortality, thrombosis, infection, and wound dehiscence. Further prospective studies across surgical populations are needed to validate these findings.

papers.abstract: Our objective was to investigate the prognostic utility of combined carbohydrate antigen (CA) 19-9 and Duke pancreatic monoclonal antigen type 2 (DUPAN-2) levels in patients undergoing curative-intent surgery for initially unresectable locally advanced (URLA) pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). Data from patients who underwent curative-intent surgery for URLA PDAC from June 2010 to December 2024 were investigated. Eligible patients were grouped into normal/normal (N/N), normal/high (N/H), high/normal (H/N), and high/high (H/H) groups according to CA19-9 and DUPAN-2 levels. Grouping was performed before and after preoperative induction chemotherapy, and survival was compared among the groups. In total, 39 patients were included. Before preoperative chemotherapy, the N/N, N/H, H/N, and H/H groups accounted for 10.3%, 20.5%, 30.8%, and 38.5%, respectively; the H/H group was the largest. After chemotherapy, the four groups accounted for 48.7%, 15.4%, 25.6%, and 10.3%, respectively; the N/N group was the largest. Pre-chemotherapy 5-year overall survival rates were 75.0%, 31.3%, 0%, and 44.9%, respectively (p = 0.427). Among the post-chemotherapy groups, the corresponding rates were 44.3%, 16.7%, 44.4%, and 0%, respectively (p < 0.001); the H/H group had significantly lower survival than the other groups. Multivariate analysis identified the post-chemotherapy H/H group as an independent predictor of poor survival (p = 0.004). Patient grouping using the two markers after preoperative chemotherapy was associated with overall survival and may be useful for prognostic stratification. In patients being considered for curative-intent surgery, the post-chemotherapy H/H group may warrant careful attention.

papers.abstract: When a radial sclerosing lesion (RSL) with associated epithelial atypia is diagnosed on image-guided core needle biopsy, current guidelines recommend complete excision to exclude malignancy. Prior studies have reported that a substantial proportion of such lesions will be 'upgraded' to malignancy when surgical excision is undertaken. More personalized management may be possible if subgroups with lower risk of harboring malignancy are identified. Following a systematic review of existing studies, we conducted an observational cohort study including all RSLs with associated atypia diagnosed on image-guided needle biopsy performed at our institution from 2020 to 2025. We estimated the cumulative incidence of malignancy at the RSL site in subgroups defined by the type of epithelial atypia and whether the atypia involved the RSL or was in the adjacent tissue. A total of 105 RSLs with associated atypia were included. Surgical excision was performed following biopsy diagnosis for 22 of 24 (91.7%) with atypical ductal hyperplasia (ADH) involving the RSL, 17 of 35 (48.6%) with ADH in the adjacent tissue, 16 of 20 (80.0%) with lobular neoplasia or other atypia involving the RSL, and 7 of 26 (26.9%) with lobular neoplasia or other atypia in the adjacent tissue. The remaining lesions underwent imaging surveillance. The cumulative incidence of malignancy at 3 years was 29.2% (95% CI: 15.1, 51.6%) for lesions with ADH involving the RSL; 8.6% (95% CI: 2.8, 24.3%) for lesions with ADH in the adjacent tissue; and 2.2% (95% CI: 0.3, 14.4%) for lesions with lobular neoplasia or other atypia. Lesions with ADH involving a RSL are likely to harbor malignancy. For other subgroups, the risk of malignancy is lower. These findings provide evidence that may be used to inform shared decision-making around imaging surveillance for selected patients with RSL and atypia on core needle biopsy.

papers.abstract: Endocrine therapy for hormone receptor-positive breast cancer is associated with adverse metabolic effects - including increased fat mass, decreased lean muscle mass, and insulin resistance - that may attenuate the efficacy of GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs). This study evaluated GLP-1 RA-associated weight loss outcomes in breast cancer patients receiving concurrent endocrine therapy. We conducted a retrospective cohort analysis of 269 breast cancer patients at a single academic center receiving concurrent GLP-1 RA and adjuvant endocrine therapy. GLP-1 RA and endocrine therapy data were obtained from electronic medication reconciliation lists and pharmacy dispense reports. Patients were required to have initiated GLP-1 therapy during the study period and to have received concurrent GLP-1 RA and endocrine therapy for at least one year. The primary outcome was percentage weight change from GLP-1 initiation to 12 months (± 2 months). Secondary outcomes included proportions achieving ≥ 5%, ≥ 10%, and ≥ 15% weight loss. Mean one-year percentage weight loss was - 4.5% (95% CI: -6.0% to - 3.0%; -3.9 kg; 95% CI: -4.96 to - 2.93 kg), significantly below the 10-20% observed in postmenopausal subgroups of GLP-1 randomized trials (all p < 0.001). Only 21.3% achieved ≥ 10% and 10.4% achieved ≥ 15% weight loss. Weight loss differed significantly by GLP-1 agent (p = 0.003); semaglutide (- 5.8%) and tirzepatide (- 4.7%) outperformed dulaglutide (+ 0.1%), which is approved for type 2 diabetes only. Higher baseline weight was associated with greater absolute loss (r = - 0.19, p = 0.002), though percentage weight loss did not differ significantly by baseline BMI category (p = 0.303). PR-negative patients lost more than PR-positive patients (- 8.2% vs. -4.2%; p = 0.021, d = 0.46). Type 2 diabetes was present in 70.6% of patients; T2DM status was not significantly associated with weight loss on t-test (p = 0.288), though patients without T2DM were numerically more likely to achieve ≥ 15% loss (21.5% vs. 5.8%). GLP-1 RAs produce statistically significant but substantially attenuated weight loss in breast cancer patients on concurrent endocrine therapy. GLP-1 agent selection significantly influences outcomes. Given emerging evidence of oncologic benefit, prospective trials are needed.

papers.abstract: The discovery of recurrent somatic mutations affecting the RNA splicing machinery in 2011 revealed an unexpected class of driver mutations in hematologic malignancies. Remarkably, splicing factor (SF) mutations have emerged as some of the most frequent genetic lesions in myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) and other dysplastic myeloid neoplasms, establishing aberrant RNA splicing as a major pathogenetic pathway in myeloid neoplasia. Subsequent studies have delineated their mutation-specific effects on RNA splicing and established their strong genotype-phenotype associations; consequently, SF mutations are now incorporated into contemporary disease classification and prognostic models. However, the mechanisms underlying their positive clonal selection and striking genotype-phenotype associations remain poorly understood, with co-mutations, clonal architecture, aging, and the hematopoietic microenvironment acting as important modifiers of disease expression. Elucidating how SF mutations interact with these modifiers to shape clonal fitness and disease phenotype remains a key challenge, while translating these biological insights into effective therapies represents the ultimate clinical goal.

papers.abstract: Donor cell-derived hematologic neoplasm (DDHN) is defined as a de novo hematologic malignancy originated from transplanted donor stem cells, distinct from the original recipient's disease (ORD). Its prevalence and biological mechanisms remain poorly defined. We conducted a nationwide study to estimate the prevalence of DDHN and characterize its clinical and molecular features. Twenty-four transplantation centers systematically reviewed their allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) cohorts. DDHN diagnosis required cytogenetic or molecular donor-origin confirmation. Molecular studies included germline-augmented targeted NGS, whole-exome sequencing, and donor-recipient comparative analyses. We identified 39 DDHN cases diagnosed between 2007 and 2025. Among 8,465 allo-HSCT performed between 2013-2022, DDHN prevalence was 0.28%, with a marked predominance after related-donor compared with unrelated transplantation (0.41% vs. 0.06%, p=0.0026). Median latency from transplantation to DDHN diagnosis was 56 months. Most DDHN were myeloid neoplasms, predominantly myelodysplastic neoplasms (51%) and acute myeloid leukemia (36%). Molecular characterization, available in 33 cases, revealed germline predisposition as the predominant underlying mechanism. Pathogenic/likely pathogenic germline variants were identified in 10 cases, involving DDX41 (n=7), CEBPA (n=2), and CHEK2 (n=1), all after a related-donor transplantation. DDX41-associated DDHN showed recurrent somatic hits and low genomic complexity. Donor-derived clonal hematopoiesis was confirmed in only one myeloid case involving U2AF1. These findings support inherited germline predisposition as the potential main molecular driver of DDHN after related allo-HSCT, reinforcing the recommendation for comprehensive germline evaluation of patients at ORD diagnosis prior to transplantation, followed by targeted cascade screening of candidate related donors.

papers.abstract: Psychedelics represent a potential breakthrough for treatment-resistant depression; however, the prolonged in-clinic monitoring required for compounds such as psilocybin and lysergic acid diethylamide is a logistical hurdle to widespread use. Intranasal mebufotenin (5-methoxy-N,N-dimethyltryptamine), a 5-hydroxytryptamine 1A (5-HT1A) and 5-HT2A agonist associated with brief psychedelic experiences, may address this limitation. To evaluate the safety, efficacy, and time to discharge readiness following a single dose of intranasal mebufotenin benzoate in adults with treatment-resistant depression. Phase 2b, randomized, double-blind trial with an 8-week blinded follow-up conducted between September 2023 and April 2025 at 38 sites in Australia, Europe, and the US. Participants were aged 18 to 75 years with moderate to severe major depressive disorder nonresponsive to 2 to 5 antidepressant trials in the current episode. The last date of follow-up was April 28, 2025. After antidepressant washout as needed, participants were randomly assigned to receive a single dose of intranasal mebufotenin benzoate, 8 mg (n = 46), 12 mg (n = 73), or 0.3 mg (a low-dose comparator; n = 74), alongside psychological support. The primary end point was total score change on the Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS; score range, 0-60; higher scores indicate more severe depression) from baseline to day 29 in the 12-mg vs 0.3-mg dose groups. Eighteen secondary end points were assessed for the 12-mg and 8-mg vs 0.3-mg doses. Discharge readiness was assessed starting 90 minutes after dosing. Among the 193 included participants, the mean age was 41 (SD, 11.1) years and 59.1% were female. From baseline to day 29, treatment with 12-mg intranasal mebufotenin benzoate vs the 0.3-mg dose (the primary end point) was associated with significantly reduced MADRS scores (mean score change, -11.1 [SD, 11.6] vs -5.5 [SD, 9.9], respectively; mean difference, -5.3 [95% CI, -8.9 to -1.8]; P = .003). The 8-mg dose also led to reduced scores from baseline to day 29 (mean score change, -12.5 [SD, 12.7]) vs the 0.3-mg dose (mean difference, -6.2 [95% CI, -10.2 to -2.1]; P = .003). MADRS reductions with the 8-mg and 12-mg doses were similar and significantly greater at all other time points from 2 to 57 days post dose vs the 0.3-mg dose. Day 29 response rates were 35%, 34%, and 12% and remission rates were 26%, 18%, and 8% in the 8-mg, 12-mg, and 0.3-mg dose groups, respectively. Treatment-emergent adverse events were reported in 76%, 85%, and 73% of participants in the 8-mg, 12-mg, and 0.3-mg dose groups, respectively; most events (99.7%) were mild or moderate. Overall, most participants were deemed ready for discharge within 2 hours post dose (85% for 8 mg and 78% for 12 mg). In adults with treatment-resistant depression, single doses of intranasal mebufotenin benzoate were well tolerated and produced rapid, robust, and durable reductions in depressive symptoms. Intranasal mebufotenin benzoate may improve treatment access and convenience, requiring a shorter monitoring period and fewer clinic visits compared with psilocybin and esketamine, respectively. papers.abstract: Distant recurrence (DR) represents a distinct and lethal trajectory in glioblastoma (GBM), characterized by the colonization of spatially isolated neural niches. The mechanisms by which disseminated tumor cells remodel the microenvironment to overcome anatomical and immunological barriers remain poorly understood. This study aimed to decode the immune ecosystem of DR and elucidate the intercellular crosstalk driving this lethal dissemination. We performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) on paired primary and DR tumor specimens from GBM patients, alongside an independent local recurrence (LR) control cohort, to map dynamic cellular shifts. Bioinformatic analyses, including differential abundance testing (Milo), cell-cell communication inference (CellChat), and copy number variation (CNV) analysis, were integrated with clinical co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) validation, bidirectional in vitro co-culture assays, and an orthotopic xenograft mouse model. Our high-resolution atlas revealed a profound remodeling of the microenvironment in DR lesions, characterized by a specific expansion of anti-inflammatory monocyte-derived tumor-associated macrophages (Anti_infl-TAM) and a paradoxical co-enrichment of CD8 + T cells and Tregs. Mechanistically, an OPC-like subpopulation of PTN+ tumor cells acted as a "paracrine architect," promoting Anti_infl-TAM polarization through the interaction between PTN and NCL. Co-IP assays confirmed direct physical binding of these two proteins in human DR tissues. Functional and bidirectional knockdown assays demonstrated that decoupling this cellular communication, achieved by targeting either PTN in tumor cells or NCL in macrophages, significantly attenuated glioma cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and macrophage polarization. In vivo, silencing PTN markedly reduced Anti_infl-TAM infiltration, suppressed intracranial tumor burden, and prolonged overall survival in tumor-bearing mice. This study establishes that DR GBM is defined by a reconfigured immune niche rather than mere genetic drift. The paracrine crosstalk between PTN+ tumor cells and Anti_infl-TAM serves as a critical engine of this permissive soil, offering a promising therapeutic target to disrupt the supportive microenvironment in distant recurrent GBM.

papers.abstract: Tracheal intubation is a physically and mentally demanding for anesthesiologists because it requires fine motor control, technical precision, rapid decision-making, situational awareness, and error avoidance. While videolaryngoscopes reduce muscle strain in normal airways, their ergonomic impact during difficult airway management remains poorly established. We aimed to compare upper limb muscle activity using dynamic surface electromyography during intubation via direct laryngoscopy (DL) vs videolaryngoscopy (VL) in simulated difficult airway scenarios. We conducted a randomized crossover trial involving 35 experienced anesthesiologists who performed tracheal intubation on a high-fidelity manikin with a normal airway, locked jaw, and rigid neck, respectively, using a Macintosh direct laryngoscope, a C-MAC® videolaryngoscope (C blade), and a King Vision® channeled videolaryngoscope. The primary outcome was upper limb muscle activity, measured by surface electromyography. Secondary outcomes included intubation time, force on upper incisors, first-attempt success rate, and perceived workload (National Aeronautics and Space Administration Task Load Index [NASA-TLX] score). Direct laryngoscopy produced significantly higher brachioradialis muscle activity than C-MAC VL in the simulated normal airway (16 vs 13 µV; median difference [MD], 3 µV; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0 to 5; P = 0.04), locked jaw (18 vs 12 µV; MD, 6 µV; 95% CI, 1 to 11; P = 0.02), and rigid neck (16 vs 13 µV; MD, 4 µV; 95% CI, 0 to 9; P = 0.03) scenarios. Direct laryngoscopy was the fastest method but exerted the highest force on the incisors (P < 0.001). King Vision VL was associated with the highest NASA-TLX workload score (P < 0.001 compared with DL), whereas C-MAC VL was least demanding. In simulated difficult airways, VL reduced upper limb muscle activity compared with DL. Nevertheless, perceived workload was higher with King Vision VL than with DL, whereas it was lower with C-MAC VL. Among the devices tested, C-MAC VL provided the most favorable ergonomic balance, combining reduced muscle strain, lower perceived workload, and highest first-attempt success rate across all airway scenarios. papers.abstract: Lenvatinib, a multi-kinase inhibitor targeting VEGFR 1–3 and FGFR 1–4, is a first-line therapy for unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). While palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia and generalized erythematous rashes are recognized side effects, lenvatinib-induced lichenoid drug reactions (LDRs) remain infrequently reported and pose significant diagnostic challenges when presenting as viral exanthematous mimics. This case describes an 82-year-old female with metastatic HCC who developed a generalized, pruritic, and vesicular rash mimicking disseminated herpes zoster shortly after initiating lenvatinib. Despite prior shingles vaccination, empiric intravenous acyclovir was initiated. A skin biopsy revealed a lichenoid dermatitis with Civatte bodies and significant eosinophilia, confirming an LDR. The eruption resolved following systemic corticosteroid therapy, indicating a likely reaction to recent lenvatinib exposure. This case highlights the importance of histopathological verification and chronological drug reconciliation in differentiating drug-induced dermatotoxicity from viral exanthems in fragile oncology populations.

papers.abstract: Aerogels are ideal materials for thermal insulation and protection. However, ceramic and carbon aerogels are generally brittle, whereas polymer aerogels often collapse and lose insulation capability under flame exposure, compromising effective thermal management across both daily use and fire emergencies. We construct a hybrid silicone aerogel with continuous silicone matrix reinforced by a silica network, enabling low thermal conductivity, excellent mechanical resilience and a unique flame-induced nano-hollowing ceramization process. Under flame, the nano-hollowing process yields an efficient thermal barrier with an unexpected decrease in thermal conductivity, enabling a 10-mm-thin panel to maintain its back-side temperature below 120 °C for at least 25 min. In addition, the aerogel provides daytime radiative cooling of 7.7 °C under midday solar irradiation. With such multifunctionality and fabrication scalability, our silicone aerogel is desirable for many strategic areas such as energy-efficient buildings and electric vehicles, where effective thermal management and sustained flame protection are greatly demanded.

papers.abstract: The efficiency of deep carbon recycling in hot subduction systems remains debated, with contrasting models predicting either extensive shallow decarbonation or substantial carbonate retention within the subducted slab. Here we present boron-isotope and geochemical data from olivine-hosted melt inclusions in volcanic arc adakites from western Panama and in forearc high-Mg andesites from SW Japan, representing modern and Archean-like hot subduction systems. Olivine-hosted melt inclusions exhibit elevated δ11B values (up to +23.2‰) coupled with high Ce/Pb, La/Yb, Eu/Ti, and Th/Zr ratios, indicating melt contributions from subducted carbonate-bearing lithologies. Integration with regional CO2 flux estimates from western Panama suggests that more than ~60% of slab carbonate escapes shallow decarbonation, likely owing to extensive forearc and arc dehydration causing substantial fluid loss, thereby suppressing fluid-mediated decarbonation beneath both the deeper forearc and arc front. These results demonstrate that substantial carbon can bypass shallow decarbonation in both modern and Archean hot subduction systems.

papers.abstract: Understanding and controlling phase transitions is fundamental to physics and central to many technological revolutions. There is currently strong interest in materials with coupled structural and electronic phase transitions, where controlling the transition plasticity naturally yields built-in memory, key for emulating neurons and synapses in neuromorphic technologies. Here, operando coherent Bragg X-ray diffraction is used to study the evolution of the nano-domain distribution at the micron-scale in neuromorphic devices made from the archetypal Mott insulator vanadium dioxide. Electrical switching leads to nano-domain reconfiguration over thousands of seconds and a jamming transition. Repetitive above-threshold currents plastically drive the system into a jammed/glassy state where switching is deterministic. Sub-threshold currents erase the short-term memory defined by the nano-domain distribution, recovering stochastic switching, thus offering a path for in-device learning. These results highlight the importance of nanoscale physics in phase transitions, even for macroscopic devices, and offer guidance for future device operation.

papers.abstract: Enantioselective construction of unnatural α-amino acids is highly desirable due to their widespread applications across biochemistry, medicinal industry and materials science. Herein, we report a straightforward and efficient method for the assembly of structurally diverse enantioenriched α-amino acid derivatives from readily accessible enamides and N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) by merging nickel hydride catalysis and hydrogen atom transfer (HAT). The protocol affords good yields and high enantioselectivities of products which easily can be converted into unprotected unnatural α-amino acids and other valuable chiral building blocks. Notably, the enantiopurity of the products can be further enhanced by normal flash chromatography on silica gel, providing a practical platform for enantiopurification of both oily and solid products. This radical cross-coupling reaction proceeds under mild conditions, tolerates a broad range of functional groups and is amenable to the construction of enantioenriched α-amino amides bearing active pharmaceutical ingredients on the sidechain.

papers.abstract: Ammonia (NH3) synthesis via nitrate reduction offers a sustainable energy conversion and mitigates aquatic NO3- pollution, yet most catalysts require high overpotentials for appreciable NH3 yields. Here, we report a sulfur-leaching strategy to transform Cu1.8S/Ru heterostructures into a small CuRu-Cu2O nanocomposite with abundant heterointerfaces, enabling strong electronic coupling between CuRu and Cu2O particles, synergistically enhancing NO3- adsorption and reaction kinetics. The optimized catalyst achieves 95.4% NH3 Faradaic efficiency at a low potential of 0.0 V versus reversible hydrogen electrode, stable over 30 cycles. Operando spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations reveal the incorporation of Ru facilitates active hydrogen generation, alleviating the energy barrier for hydrogenation steps at heterointerfaces. The catalyst demonstrates high stability in a membrane electrode assembly at 450 mA cm-2 over 200 h and enables a Zinc-NO3- battery operation exceeding 50 h, offering a design model for durable, active nanocomposites in sustainable NH3 synthesis.

papers.abstract: The ClpXP ATP-dependent unfoldase-protease complex plays important roles in maintaining protein homeostasis in the mitochondria. Pathogenic variants of CLPP have been identified in patients with Perrault syndrome type 3 (PRLTS3), a rare recessive mitochondrial disease characterized by sensorineural hearing loss, ovarian dysfunction, and neurological abnormalities. However, it remains unclear how these ClpP variants cause this disease. Here we identify three cellular substrates of ClpXP using proteomic analysis of PRLTS3 patient-derived fibroblasts, with follow up studies using induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) and iPSC-derived neural progenitor cells, alongside in vitro biochemical assays. These substrates are: CHCHD2, a bi-organellar regulator of oxidative phosphorylation and mitochondrial stress responses; ALAS1, which catalyzes the rate-limiting step in heme biosynthesis; and TFAM, an essential mitochondrial transcription factor. Efficient degradation of these substrates by ClpXP requires the adaptor protein PDIP38. We propose that dysregulated cellular levels of these substrates might contribute to the etiology of PRLTS3.

papers.abstract: Trimerization motifs play pivotal roles in structural biology and therapeutic protein engineering. Here, we describe a short trimerization motif (rFd1303) derived from the Reoviridae family reovirus σ1 protein. Compared with the widely used T4-Foldon, the rFd1303 increased recombinant protein yields. The rFd1303-fused immunogens of SARS-CoV-2 spike and influenza hemagglutinin elicited antibody responses comparable to T4-Foldon-fused controls in mice. Using this tag, we engineered a trimeric ACE2-Ig fusion protein (TriACE2-Ig) that remained stable after 30 days at room temperature and neutralized a broad range of ACE2-utilizing sarbecoviruses, including 19 SARS-CoV-2 variants, SARS-CoV, and pangolin coronaviruses GD and GX, with higher potency than monomeric ACE2-Ig. In the hamster model challenged with various SARS-CoV-2 variants, our data demonstrated that intranasal TriACE2-Ig administration markedly reduced viral loads, virus-induced body-weight loss, lung pathology, and decreased within-cage virus transmission. These findings highlight rFd1303 as a versatile trimerization platform for vaccine and therapeutic protein development.

papers.abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) demands high-performance hardware accelerators. Photonic computing with microring resonators (MRRs) has attracted significant interest, but conventional architectures use MRRs primarily as scalar weights, with speed constrained by the resonance linewidth of ~ 10 GHz. Here, we redefine MRRs as programmable temporal convolution kernels by exploiting their impulse responses, enabling computation beyond the resonance linewidth. A single MRR operating at a symbol rate of 128 Gbaud achieves a computing throughput of 5.12 trillion operations per second (TOPS), representing a 160-fold improvement over scalar weighting. By integrating temporal convolution with wavelength- and space-division multiplexing, we realize a multi-channel MRR convolution engine with 120.8 TOPS throughput and reduce the hardware complexity from O(N2) to O(N), achieving a compute density of 48.05 TOPS/mm2. The framework is experimentally validated through optical modulation format identification, network anomaly detection, and image classification, establishing a scalable computing primitive for photonic AI accelerators.

papers.abstract: Opportunities remain to leverage population structure in large scale genomic studies for additional insight. Admixture mapping (AM) identifies loci where disease risk differs by ancestral background, offering a complementary strategy to genome-wide association studies (GWAS) in admixed populations. We performed a systematic comparison of AM and GWAS across over 800 clinical phenotypes in Hispanic/Latino (HL) and African American (AA) participants from the BioMe biobank. We developed a well-calibrated AM pipeline tailored to the local ancestry structure of HL (N = 14,876) and AA (N = 8,819). While GWAS identified a greater number of significant associations, AM revealed 77 signals, including 48 not detected by GWAS. AM-tagged variants had higher minor allele frequency and population differentiation (Fst), while GWAS demonstrated higher odds ratios, underscoring the distinct genetic architecture identified by each method. This study emphasizes the importance of applying both GWAS and AM approaches to uncover previously unreported loci in admixed populations.

papers.abstract: Tropical cyclone post-landfall decay strongly influences inland hazard exposure, yet most studies assume that environmental change affects storms of different intensities uniformly. Here we identify an intensity-dependent divergence in global trends of tropical cyclone post-landfall decay. Analyzing 885 observed events (1979-2024), we show that strong storms (≥29 m/s) now weaken 18.6% faster after landfall, whereas weak storms persist 14.5% longer inland. These contrasting trends arise from different environmental sensitivities. Weak storms respond primarily to thermodynamic factors, including sea-surface warming, enhanced atmospheric moisture, and increased oceanic influence along storm tracks, all of which favor prolonged inland persistence. In contrast, strong storms are more sensitive to dynamic and land-surface conditions, including faster translation speeds, increasing atmospheric stability, and drier soil, which collectively promote faster decay. Numerical experiments further demonstrate that weaker storms respond more strongly to thermodynamic enhancement, whereas stronger storms are more vulnerable to dynamic disruption. These results challenge uniform-response assumptions in tropical cyclone risk assessment, forging a dual-threat landscape: intensifying coastal impacts from faster-decaying strong storms alongside expanding inland risks from increasingly persistent weak systems. Our findings reveal pronounced intensity-dependent heterogeneity in tropical cyclones, urging refined hazard assessment and adaptation for vulnerable and unprepared regions worldwide.

papers.abstract: Non-Hermitian systems host a wealth of exotic phenomena, yet their temporal topology-particularly in time-reversal-symmetry-broken conditions-remains largely unexplored. Here, we experimentally demonstrate topological memory emerging from hysteresis-driven dynamics in a nonreciprocal microwave scattering system. The scattering singularity, encompassing both backscattering zeros and nonreciprocal exceptional points (EPs), serves as the cornerstone of this effect. Magnetic hysteresis induces a history-dependent trajectory of the complex scattering parameter that winds around such singularities, giving rise to quantized topological charges and sharp transitions when crossing them. At the limit of infinite nonreciprocity, backscattering zeros facilitate access to EPs, drastically easing their realization and yielding enhanced frequency combs near the transition. Extending these dynamics to free-space broadcasting and circulator-based topological insulators, we demonstrate nonreciprocity-assisted transport and long-distance preservation of scattering singularities. Our results uncover the interplay among singularity, nonreciprocity, and Floquet engineering, establishing a unified platform for exploring temporal topology and in-memory non-Hermitian photonics.

papers.abstract: Hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) plays a crucial role in environmental remediation, chemical synthesis, and energy storage. Nevertheless, its industrial production is energy consuming with significant environmental burdens. Here we show a proof-of-concept thermoelectrocatalytic strategy for H2O2 production directly from seawater, driven solely by low-grade waste heat. A low-temperature thermoelectric (TE) material, Na- and Pb-codoped SnSe, is designed as a catalyst that enables efficient H2O2 generation under a moderate temperature gradient (ΔT). This system achieves an H2O2 production rate of 6.1 mmol g-1 h-1 from seawater under ΔT = 120 K, which is competitive with the representative photocatalytic systems. Experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that Na/Pb-codoping improves the TE properties, promotes charge carrier migration under ΔT, and promotes the oxygen reduction reaction toward H2O2 formation. The naturally formed strong electric layer at the catalyst-seawater interface further promotes both reaction kinetics and thermodynamic driving forces. Our finding provides a sustainable route for H2O2 production from seawater using waste heat and demonstrates great potential of TE-catalysis for waste heat utilization.

papers.abstract: 2D magnetic semiconductors, which intrinsically couple a rich landscape of magnetic orders with tightly bound electron-hole pairs (excitons), present an exciting platform to investigate the interplay between optical and magnetic phenomena at the atomic scale. In such systems, the strength of magneto-optical effects determines how deeply the magnetic properties can be revealed. Here, we report the observation of remarkably strong magneto-optical effects in the 2D magnetic semiconductor CrSBr that allow probing its magnetic order with unprecedented sensitivity. By investigating optical transitions above the fundamental exciton energy, we discover massive spectral red- and blueshifts approaching 100 meV under applied magnetic fields - an order of magnitude larger than previously observed magneto-excitonic responses. Our comprehensive magneto-optical experiments, accompanied by detailed DFT calculations, indicate the possible origin of the transitions exhibiting such intriguing behavior. These findings open avenues for exploiting magneto-optical phenomena in newly accessible regimes, enabling novel opto-spintronic applications previously limited by weak magnetic responses.

papers.abstract: Direct photolithography offers a transformative photoresist-free route for high-precision integration in electronic and optoelectronic platforms. Despite significant advancements in quantum dots (QDs), existing methods often degrade optoelectronic performance due to the inherent surface ligand changes during photolithographic processing. Here, we introduce a reversible photolithography strategy to overcome this bottleneck. This strategy is based on the first wavelength-gated, reversible ligand crosslinking and decrosslinking cycle, enabling the dynamic and reversible control over the photolithographic process. Using this approach, we achieve high-efficient and high-fidelity QD photolithography with restored QD structure and functionality. The reversible process further enables high-performance electroluminescence, with one of the highest luminance values of 125,016 cd m-2 at 5.0 V and a peak external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 24.41%. Moreover, we demonstrate an ultrahigh-resolution nano-pixelated device with a peak EQE of 17.08% at 21,000 PPI. This work presents a photo-reversible crosslinking system that decouples photolithographic patterning from performance degradation, offering a versatile platform for high-end QD-based displays and other advanced optoelectronics.

papers.abstract: Abstract Background Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is one of the most aggressive malignancies and is characterized by a high degree of heterogeneity. However, HCC treatment remains difficult, highlighting the need to better define molecular subgroups of HCC and understand their potential relationships with therapeutic response. Methods In this study, we established 20 patient‐derived organoids and 12 patient‐derived cell lines from 20 individuals diagnosed with HCC. These models were comprehensively characterized using whole‐exome sequencing, RNA sequencing, drug screening, and hepatitis B virus (HBV)‐targeting PCR with a focus on HBV‐related HCC. Results Based on transcriptomic profiling, this study classified HCC into two molecular subtypes, aligning with previously reported classifications. Drug screening revealed that the greater enrichment of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signalling pathway was associated with increased sensitivity to everolimus and lenvatinib. Integrated transcriptomic and drug‐response analyses further identified candidate genes associated with lenvatinib response. In addition, polymerase chain reaction (PCR) analysis targeting the HBV surface, core, and X genes demonstrated noticeable discrepancies relative to the clinically reported HBV infection status. Notably, HBV DNA detection was associated with activation of the calcium signalling pathway and oxaliplatin response. Conclusions This study provides a valuable resource for investigating the biology and pharmacological characteristics of HCC, particularly in the context of molecular subtypes and HBV‐associated mechanisms. Ultimately, these findings offer additional insights into HCC heterogeneity and drug response and may serve as a basis for further investigation of molecular determinants of therapeutic response.

papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Histological subtype and resection completeness are established prognostic factors in retroperitoneal liposarcoma, but evidence often derives from resected primary disease. We characterized management and post-referral survival in a referral cohort. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 61 patients managed from May 2015 to September 2025. Overall survival (OS) was measured from first presentation at our center. Kaplan–Meier and exploratory Cox analyses were performed, allowing the association between tumor diameter and mortality to vary over time. Results: Forty-two patients had primary disease, and 19 had recurrent disease; 12 had well-differentiated liposarcoma (WDLPS), and 49 had dedifferentiated liposarcoma (DDLPS). Among 24 patients who underwent surgery, 21 had macroscopically complete (R0/R1) resection. Twenty-five patients died. No deaths occurred in WDLPS; median OS was 29.8 months in DDLPS (p = 0.008). In DDLPS, recurrent versus primary disease was not associated with OS (hazard ratio [HR], 0.99; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.41–2.38). Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status ≥ 2 (n = 6 in the entire cohort) was associated with poorer OS (adjusted HR, 8.03; 95% CI, 2.20–29.36), and the association between tumor diameter and mortality varied over time (adjusted interaction HR, 1.44; 95% CI, 1.07–1.95). Conclusions: Observed post-referral survival differed by histological subtype. Among patients with DDLPS, no survival difference between primary and recurrent disease was demonstrated, but the wide CI and referral-related survivor selection preclude an inference of equivalence. Associations involving performance status and time-varying tumor diameter were exploratory and require external validation.

papers.abstract: Lorlatinib is a third-generation anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK)/ROS1 tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) that has been shown to have high efficacy in the first line setting for treatment of advanced ALK-rearranged non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, some adverse events have been described that require proper follow-up and management to obtain the maximum benefit from treatment and minimize risk to the patient. These include dyslipidemia and weight gain, conditions that in Latin America have a high prevalence in the general population, which coupled with limitations in timely access to specialized care, could influence both manifestation and management. The objective of this consensus is to provide recommendations tailored to our real-world setting that will optimize the monitoring and early management of toxicities in patients treated with lorlatinib in Latin America.

papers.abstract: Background Zoledronic acid is used to prevent skeletal complications in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) and bone metastases. Real world data on its use in resource-limited setting, particularly in sub-saharan Africa, remain scarce. Aim To describe clinical outcomes, skeletal-related events, safety and quality of life in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) and bone metastases treated with zoledronic acid in Côte d’Ivoire. Methods We conducted a retrospective, single center cohort study including 144 patients with mCRPC and bone metastases treated with zoledronic acid at Treichville university Hospital between January 2019 and December 2021. The primary endpoint was skeletal event-free survival (SEFS) defined as the time from the first zoledronic acid administration to the first on-treatment skeletal related event (SRE). Patients without an SRE were censored at their last available follow-up. Results The median age was 67 years (range: 42–91), and 133 patients (92.4%) were older than 50 years. Before zoledronic acid initiation, 59 patients (41.0%) had experienced at least one skeletal-related event. After treatment initiation, 30 patients (20.8%) experienced at least one new on-treatment SRE, whereas 114 (79.2%) did not. Among patients who experienced an SRE, the median time to the first event was 9 months (range 5-11). Median SEFS was not reached and the estimated 12-month SEFS was 79.2%. The most frequently documented adverse events were bone pain (18.8%), constipation (18.1%) and nausea (9.7%). FACT-G data at both baseline and 12-month were available for 129 patients (89.6%) and mean scores across all four FACT-G domains, as well as the total FACT-G score, were numerically lower at 12 months than at baseline. Conclusion In this retrospective cohort of patients with mCRPC and bone metastases, 20.8% experienced a new SRE after zoledronic acid initiation, while median SEFS was not reached. FACT-G scores decreased during follow-up. These findings provide real-world data on zoledronic acid use in a resource-limited setting.

papers.abstract: Objective Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is a leading cause of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Conventional biomarkers alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) and des-gamma-carboxy prothrombin (DCP) have diagnostic limitations, particularly for early-stage disease. This study investigated the expression profile of ORC1 in HBV-related liver disease and its association with HBV infection, disease progression, and prognosis. Methods 178 participants were recruited: 124 HBV-positive cases (49 HBV-HCC, 33 HBV-cirrhosis, 42 chronic hepatitis B) and 54 HBV-negative controls (35 non-HBV-HCC, 19 hepatic hemangioma). Tissue ORC1 was detected by immunohistochemistry, and serum ORC1 was measured by ELISA in a subset of 17 HBV-HCC patients with available serum. Logistic regression identified factors associated with high ORC1 expression. ROC curves were used to evaluate the discrimination of tissue ORC1, AFP, and DCP for HBV-HCC, and the correlation between ORC1 and tumor diameter was analyzed. TCGA-LIHC data were used for external validation. Results Tissue ORC1 was significantly upregulated in HBV-positive patients, and HBV infection was independently associated with high ORC1 expression (P<0. 001). ORC1 expression increased progressively from chronic hepatitis B to cirrhosis to HCC. In a subset of 17 HBV-HCC patients with available serum, tissue and serum ORC1 were moderately correlated (Spearman rs=0. 554, 95% CI 0. 085–0. 822, P = 0. 021). Tissue ORC1 showed moderate discrimination between HBV-HCC and HBV-LC (AUC = 0. 64) and between HBV-HCC and CHB (AUC = 0. 66). ORC1 expression was not significantly associated with tumor diameter ( P >0. 05). High ORC1 expression was associated with poorer overall survival in TCGA-LIHC (HR = 1. 7, P = 0. 0026). Conclusion ORC1 upregulation is independently associated with HBV infection and increases with disease progression in HBV-related liver disease. Although tissue ORC1 showed only moderate discrimination for HBV-HCC, high ORC1 expression was associated with poorer overall survival in TCGA-LIHC. These findings suggest that ORC1 is primarily a proliferation- and progression-related marker in HBV-related liver disease.

papers.abstract: Background BI-RADS category 4 breast lesions are suspicious and generally undergo tissue diagnosis, but malignancy risk remains heterogeneous across BI-RADS 4A, 4B, and 4C. We developed and internally validated an interpretable mammography-based model for risk stratification within this diagnostic category. Methods This single-center retrospective diagnostic prediction study included 441 patients, each contributing one index BI-RADS 4 mammographic lesion. Outcomes were verified histopathologically in 397 lesions and by longitudinal imaging stability in 44. Three primary models and a sensitivity model excluding BI-RADS were evaluated. Internal validation used 1,000 paired patient-level bootstrap resamples in which imputation, encoding, standardization, penalty selection, LASSO selection, and coefficient estimation were repeated. Results Of 441 lesions, 165 were malignant. Malignancy rates were 15.7% (34/216), 46.4% (70/151), and 82.4% (61/74) in BI-RADS 4A, 4B, and 4C, respectively. The final model retained BI-RADS 4B, BI-RADS 4C, architectural distortion, circularity-deficit irregularity score, contour serration score, and normalized GLCM contrast. Optimism-corrected AUCs were 0.770 (95% CI, 0.729-0.815) for BI-RADS only, 0.774 (0.733-0.814) for clinical plus BI-RADS, and 0.841 (0.809-0.877) for the full mammography-based model. Clinical variables did not improve validated performance. The full model improved corrected AUC versus BI-RADS only by 0.072 (0.028-0.108) and versus clinical plus BI-RADS by 0.067 (0.029-0.103). Its corrected calibration intercept was 0.002 (-0.209 to 0.208) and slope was 1.445 (1.140-1.753). Within-category AUCs were 0.785, 0.721, and 0.758 for BI-RADS 4A, 4B, and 4C; the pathology-only corrected AUC was 0.835 (0.799-0.871). Conclusion Structured and quantitative mammographic features improved internally validated discrimination and within-category risk stratification beyond BI-RADS subcategory alone. Because predicted risks were under-dispersed and validation was limited to one center, the model should be used only as a research-stage risk-stratification and prioritization tool, not to replace biopsy. External validation and recalibration are required before clinical implementation.
